items.title: Import failures are reported as raw Dart exception text ('Import failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 1)')
items.reasoning: Everything the summary names is in the tree and correctly wired (profile_export_data.dart:5/11 kProfileExportFormat + kProfileExportVersion, :29 profileExportEnvelope, :47 profilesFromExportDocument, :146 parseExportedProfile; profile_service.dart:540/... both exports write the envelope; screen_shell.dart:42 describeProfileImportFailure called at :710). As SHIPPED BY THE FIXER the fix left two holes that reproduce the exact defect the finding names, both now closed in the tree by the earlier verify pass and independently re-confirmed by me: (a) the self-identifying envelope does not fire for the wrong file an operator actually picks, because a Skotiq SEQUENCE export carries no 'format' key and a STRING '2.0' version, and the legacy bare-map branch accepted any map merely containing 'name' - so a sequence file (sitting in the same folder, offered by the same .json picker) was silently imported as a profile with focalLength/aperture 0; (b) ProfileExportData.fromJson read its ~25 optional fields with bare 'as String?' casts, which throw TypeError, not FormatException, so a hand-edited or foreign document still reached the operator as "type 'int' is not a subtype of type 'String?' in type cast". The current file closes both: :95 rejects a sequence document by name, :107 requires one of _legacyProfileFields (:120) alongside 'name', :599-667 are typed readers raising FormatException, and :165 is a catch-all that logs the raw error and shows prose. Residual nits, not verdict-changing: describeProfileImportFailure only substitutes the file name into messages that literally start 'That file', so the newer-version message keeps the generic subject; and a failure inside _createProfileFromExport (duplicate name, host HTTP error) still reaches the operator through the 'Could not import "x.json": $e' branch, which the code documents as deliberate.
items.evidence: Call-site severance (mine, this pass): replaced screen_shell.dart:710 'describeProfileImportFailure(e, fileName: pickedFileName)' with "'Import failed: $e'" and re-ran the suite - equipment_profile_import_authority_test.dart went red on BOTH 'a rejected import names the picked file, not a Dart exception' [E] and 'profile import reports failures and unlocks retry' [E]; restored and all 20 tests across the eight settings suites pass. I also verified there is exactly one production import surface: grep for profilesFromExportDocument/parseExportedProfile/importProfileFromJson finds only profile_service.dart, the settings screen, and equipment_screen's delete-undo (which round-trips exportProfileToJson, i.e. the new envelope, and is covered by the envelope branch).
items.repairSummary: The substantive repair (sequence-document rejection, _legacyProfileFields gate, typed field readers, catch-all prose) was landed by the earlier verify pass and is present and tested in packages/skotiq_core/test/services/profile_export_format_test.dart; I re-verified it rather than re-doing it. My own repair this pass: that pass left packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart unformatted (a stray blank line inside the describeProfileImportFailure call at :711), which fails the repo's `dart format` launch gate. Ran dart format on the file; the only change is that blank line.

items.title: About shows 6.1.0 but drops the build number, and System Information omits everything a support ticket needs
items.reasoning: Read the file rather than the summary. about_settings.dart:243 renders 'Version ${appVersion.version} (build ${appVersion.buildNumber})' (and :505 in the licence card), so the already-closed half is genuinely closed. systemInformationProvider (:328) emits Skotiq version+build, Platform, OS version, Dart, 'Connected to' ('imaging host <serverHost>' for a NetworkBackend, else 'this computer') and 'Database schema', each fact individually guarded so a missing provider drops one line instead of the card; skotiqDataFolderProvider (:376) is a separate FutureProvider whose value is appended only when it resolves, so the card paints on the first frame as claimed; the Copy button writes 'label: value' lines to the clipboard; _SystemInformationCard is mounted in the real page at :299, in the column both the mobile and desktop layouts use. Layout risk checked because a Row-header overflow is this wave's known regression shape: the header is Expanded title + small outline button, and each fact renders through SettingsInfoRow (settings_link_and_info_rows.dart:83), whose value sits in an Expanded Text with no maxLines - so a long OS version or data path soft-wraps rather than overflowing. The abstention on a Rust bridge version is honest (nothing in the Dart layer exposes one). One nit I record without flipping the verdict: on a remote client 'Database schema' is THIS client's schema printed directly under 'Connected to: imaging host X', which a support reader can easily take for the host's.
items.evidence: Severed the wiring myself: commented out 'const _SystemInformationCard(),' at about_settings.dart:299 - about_system_information_test.dart went 1 passed / 2 failed ('the block names the build, the schema and the data folder' [E] and 'Copy puts the whole block on the clipboard' [E]) while the provider-only test stayed green, which is the correct split. Restored from a byte copy (never git checkout): 20/20 green across the eight settings suites.

items.title: Replay & Debug is written for the developer who built it: a lowercase title sentence and two user-facing dialogs that name a database table
items.reasoning: All four counts check out in replay_debug_settings.dart. (1) SettingsPage title is 'Replay & Debug' (:107) with a sentence-cased, remote-aware description of what the retention window is for. (2) A repo-wide grep for 'sequence_decisions' returns only schema/migration/model comments and one test assertion that the string is absent - no user-facing string names the table. (3) The confirmation asks the authority how much it is about to destroy BEFORE asking for consent (:242) and branches three ways on null / 1 / N (:248-258). The chain is real end to end and I read each link: ReplayDebugService.countAll(), handleCountDecisions (replay_debug_handlers.dart:58) which returns the unfiltered count only when 'runId' is absent so the existing per-run callers are untouched, NetworkBackend.replayCountAllDecisions(), and ReplayDebugSettingsController.countAllHistory() (replay_debug_provider.dart:405) which catches every error and returns null - important, because the screen awaits it with no try/catch and a throw would strand _isClearing true and brick the button. (4) ConfirmDialog.show(..., confirmLabel: 'Clear history', isDestructive: true). Pre-existing nit unchanged by the fix: _isClearing is set true before the count, so the button reads 'Clearing...' while it is only counting, and the remote round-trip lengthens that window. (The page title is hard-coded English while the settings entry it must match is localised - 'Reproduccion y depuracion' in es - so the 'matching' claim is true only in English; that is the product-wide convention for settings page bodies, not something this fix introduced.)
items.evidence: Severed the count wiring myself: replaced 'final total = await c.countAllHistory();' with 'final int? total = null;'. replay_debug_clear_confirmation_test.dart 'the confirmation states how many decisions it will delete' went red [E]; the authority test (which forces the null fallback deliberately) correctly stayed green. Restored: 20/20 green across the eight settings suites. apps/desktop/test/headless_api/replay_debug_handlers_test.dart already covers both the runId-filtered and the unfiltered form of the endpoint.

items.title: Seven paired devices are all called 'Android companion' with no way to tell them apart before revoking
items.reasoning: pairing_screen.dart:751 renders _AccessBadge(grantSpec: device.authGrantSpec) beside the device-type label inside a Wrap (so it cannot overflow the row), and _AccessBadge (:1152) maps admin -> 'Full access' in colors.warning, control -> 'Can control the rig', view -> 'View only', anything else -> 'Custom access', with the raw spec on the Tooltip. I checked the two things that could have made this cosmetic. First, the value is the stored one: the list is _tokenManager.getActivePairedDevices(), i.e. the PairedDevice drift row, and paired_devices_table.dart:38 declares authGrantSpec non-nullable defaulting to 'control', so no row renders an empty badge. Second - the failure mode that would have made this RELOCATED rather than fixed - I checked what the host actually stores, because if real pairings persisted the fine-grained form every row would read 'Custom access' and the list would be uniform again: HeadlessAuthGrant.toSpec() (auth_policy.dart:355) canonicalises back to 'admin'/'control'/'view' whenever the grant covers every resource at one level, and pairing_handlers.dart:506 pairs at 'control', so the coarse badges are what real rows get. This is also the only paired-device list surface in the product (grep for getActivePairedDevices finds only this screen). One thing I checked and then withdrew as a finding: the badge labels are hard-coded English while sibling strings in that row go through context.l10n, but every settings page body in the product is hard-coded English (appearance_settings.dart, adaptive_exposure_settings.dart, etc.), so the badge follows the existing convention rather than introducing a gap.
items.evidence: Severed the wiring myself: commented out the _AccessBadge line in the device row - pairing_access_badge_test.dart 'each paired device shows what its token is allowed to do' went red [E]; restored, green. The test builds three otherwise byte-identical 'Android companion' rows in a real in-memory PairingDatabase with admin / view / fine-grained specs, so it also fails a badge that always prints the same word, not merely a missing one.

items.title: Paired devices cannot be renamed, and nothing records which device on the network a row is
items.reasoning: Every named piece exists and is connected, and the motivation is real: mobile_pairing_service.dart:49-57 does return a per-platform constant ('Android companion' for every Android device), so the schema's stated intent for device_name is unreachable by any operator action. PairingDatabase.renamePairedDevice (pairing_database.dart:152) returns the update's row count; TokenManager.renameDevice (token_manager.dart:322) is exactly '_database.renamePairedDevice(...) > 0' and touches nothing else, so sessionToken / authGrantSpec / expiresAt are untouched and a device mid-run is not disturbed; PairingNotifier.renameDevice (pairing_screen.dart:355) trims, refuses an empty name before any write, runs inside the same _enqueue/mounted/generation discipline as revoke and delete, and on a 0-row result reloads the list and returns false rather than claiming a rename; the row popup menu has a 'rename' entry (:800) opening _RenameDeviceDialog (:1064), whose field is autofocus, pre-filled with the current name, commits on Return, disables Save while the trimmed text is empty, and surfaces pairingErrorRename on failure. Two residuals I record, neither contradicting the claim: TokenManager.completePairing deletes and re-inserts the row, so deliberately re-pairing that handset resets the operator's chosen name back to 'Android companion'; and _enqueue returns false while any other pairing operation is in flight, so a rename attempted during a concurrent revoke reports the generic rename error rather than 'busy'. Verified by reading and by a widget test that drives the real notifier against a real in-memory PairingDatabase - not against a live paired appliance, which this host-database path does not require.
items.evidence: Severed the write myself: replaced 'if (!await _tokenManager.renameDevice(deviceId, name))' with 'if (!await Future<bool>.value(true))', which keeps the UI flow intact but never touches the database - pairing_rename_device_test.dart 'a paired device can be renamed, and the new name persists' went red [E] while the empty-name test stayed green (correct: that path never reaches the write). Restored, green. The test asserts the STORED row and that the sibling row and the token/grant are unchanged, so a rename that only repainted would fail it.

items.title: 'Restore' asks you to restart the app afterwards but does not offer to, and nothing on the screen stays to remind you
items.reasoning: The banner is real and both restore paths reach it - backup_screen.dart _announceRestore is called from the listed-backup path (remote and local branches) and from the imported-file path, with the imaging-host wording keyed off `backend is NetworkBackend`; the restore success snackbar is genuinely gone (the remaining showSuccessSnackBar calls are for backup creation and delete). But the fixer's own falsifiable claim - 'it stays until the operator presses Dismiss', 'the operator now cannot lose the message' - was not true as shipped. `_restoreNotice` was a field on the screen's State, so the banner was cleared by LEAVING the page, which is precisely the next thing the operator does: the premise of the finding is that you restore because you are about to observe, so the very next action is walking to Imaging to start the run, and that action silently cancelled the reminder. The message therefore survived time (the fixer's test pumps 30 s) but not navigation - the defect moved from 'a snackbar that fades in five seconds' to 'a banner that dies when you navigate', which is this campaign's RELOCATED shape dressed as a fix. Repaired below. The declined 'Restart now' button is a defensible, explicitly-stated product decision, not a hidden gap, and I do not hold it against the entry. Not verifiable without a live host: in remote mode the text asks the operator to restart the imaging HOST, which this app cannot confirm happened.
items.evidence: Proved by reading (`String? _restoreNotice;` was screen State, cleared on dispose) and then by test: with the fixer's original file restored, the new test 'the restart reminder survives leaving and re-entering the page' fails [E] (1 passed, 1 failed) while the original 'survives the snackbar' test passes - i.e. the existing test could not see the defect. Call-site severance (mine): commented out `_announceRestore(result.itemsRestored, remote: false);` in the listed-backup local branch - backup_restore_notice_test.dart went red while backup_import_authority_test.dart stayed GREEN, which proves the two restore paths are independently covered (the earlier pass severed the other one and got the mirror result). Restored from byte copies; both files green.
items.repairSummary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart: moved the notice out of State into a new `restoreRestartNoticeProvider` (StateProvider<String?>) declared in the same file, watched in build and cleared only by the Dismiss button. In-memory on purpose: a restart is what resolves the condition, so a restart clears the notice for free, and nothing is persisted. Added 'the restart reminder survives leaving and re-entering the page' to packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/backup_restore_notice_test.dart, which restores, swaps the widget tree to an unrelated screen under the SAME ProviderScope (disposing BackupScreen's State exactly as the settings shell does), re-enters, and asserts the banner is still there and that Dismiss - and only Dismiss - clears it. It fails against the pre-repair file. dart format + dart analyze clean.

items.title: A 426 MB abandoned GLADE download sat in the catalog directory for six weeks with nothing in the UI acknowledging it
items.reasoning: The sweep exists and is wired: CatalogManager.initialize() (manager.dart:93) awaits _sweepAbandonedPartials(dir) after creating the directory and before prewarmSearchCaches(), deleting each leftover and logging the MB reclaimed, with per-file and whole-scan try/catch so a locked leftover cannot fail startup. As SHIPPED it swept only the top level for '.partial', which missed the third downloader in the same tree: deep_star_catalog.dart:310 writes '${target.path}.part' into the catalogDirectory/deep_stars SUBdirectory, the identical unresumable-leftover defect one level down. That gap was closed by the earlier verify pass (recursive listing + a named suffix set) and I re-confirmed it. Two things I checked independently that the fixer's 'safe and complete' claim depends on. First, coverage on the machine that actually leaks: the appliance runs main_headless, and it does call initialiseCatalogManager (main_headless.dart:263), the same function as the GUI (main.dart:230) - so the sweep is not GUI-only. Second, the suffix set cannot eat a real file: grep for every '.partial'/'.part' writer finds annotation_catalog_io.dart:56, legacy_catalog_io.dart:70/456, unified_catalog_api.dart:209 and deep_star_catalog.dart:310, all temporaries under the catalog directory, and stack_share_export_service.dart:157 which writes '<name>.partial.png' OUTSIDE the catalog tree and ends in .png, so it is not matched. Residual worth recording, not repaired because it is speculative and would need a lock design: the sweep assumes it is the only process using that directory, so a GUI instance starting while a headless host on the same machine is mid-download would delete the live '.partial'.
items.evidence: Severed the production call myself: commented out 'await _sweepAbandonedPartials(dir);' in initialize() - catalog_partial_sweep_test.dart went 0 passed / 2 failed ('initialize reclaims an abandoned partial download' [E] and 'a deep-star tile leftover in a subdirectory is reclaimed' [E]); restored and both pass. The subdirectory test is the one that fails if the recursion or the '.part' suffix is taken back out.
items.repairSummary: The recursive '.partial'/'.part' sweep and its subdirectory test were landed by the earlier verify pass (manager.dart:104-160, packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/catalog_partial_sweep_test.dart); I re-verified them by severance rather than re-doing the edit.

blockedOnSharedCode: The restart reminder is still only visible on Settings > Backup & Restore. The condition it describes ('this app is showing the state it had before the restore') applies to every screen, and the operator's next stop is Imaging. Surfacing it as an app-level banner would mean editing the shared app shell/scaffold (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/... shell + the desktop/mobile navigation chrome), which other areas own; restoreRestartNoticeProvider in backup_screen.dart is already the right source for it, so the shell change is a one-line watch.
